shower.thought: You've never actually experienced the color blue—only your brain's interpretation of a specific wavelength.
We spend our lives running from boredom, but boredom might be the only time our brains are actually processing who we are.
Every person you've ever met has a version of you in their head that has nothing to do with who you actually are.
Nostalgia is just grief wearing a prettier mask.
You can't remember most of your life, so you're essentially living with an unreliable narrator who's pretending to be you.
The fear of wasting time is often what wastes the most time.
Mirrors show you what you look like, but they've never shown you how you actually appear to other people.
We preserve dead people's words as wisdom, but we ignore the same thoughts when living people say them.
Your body is replacing itself constantly, but everyone still holds you accountable for what your old body did.
The most productive people you know probably feel like they're constantly falling behind.
We call it "finding ourselves" but we're usually just finding the version we wish we were and hoping it sticks.
Silence in a conversation means something different depending on whether you like the person.
You've probably had profound thoughts you'll never remember, while you can't forget completely mundane ones.
The reason we're afraid of death might just be that we're afraid of not mattering.
Social media didn't create fake people—it just gave real people a stage to perform who they already were in private.
Most arguments aren't really about the topic—they're about whether the other person thinks you're worth listening to.
We assume confident people know something we don't, but they might just be better at acting like uncertainty doesn't exist.
Your default setting is to believe what you hear first, then you spend energy convincing yourself to doubt it.
The saddest part of outgrowing people isn't the distance—it's realizing they haven't changed at all.
You can't actually imagine something you've never experienced; you can only remix things you have.

motivational.thought: The person you become through your actions is the only version of you that actually exists. — Unknown
Every moment you're not moving toward what matters is a moment you're moving away from it. — Unknown
Your obstacles are not punishment—they're the curriculum. — Unknown
The only difference between who you are and who you want to be is the decisions you make when no one is watching. — Unknown
Waiting for the right moment is just procrastination wearing a disguise. — Unknown
You can't think your way into a new life. You have to live your way into it. — Unknown
The person who says it can't be done is usually interrupted by someone doing it. — Unknown
What feels impossible today becomes your standard tomorrow if you keep showing up. — Unknown
Discipline is just choosing what you want most over what you want now. — Unknown
You're not behind. You're exactly where your choices have taken you. — Unknown
The life you're designing in your head means nothing without the life you're building with your hands. — Unknown
Small progress repeated is more powerful than perfect action postponed. — Unknown
Your potential isn't hiding—it's waiting for you to stop making excuses. — Unknown
The only real failure is the failure to try. Everything else is just data. — Unknown
What makes you uncomfortable is usually what makes you grow. — Unknown
You don't attract what you want. You attract who you are. — Unknown
The gap between knowing and doing is where most dreams die. — Unknown
Your future self is watching you right now. Make them proud. — Unknown
Pressure either breaks you or builds you. The difference is your choice. — Unknown
The best time to plant a tree was yesterday. The second best time is today. — Ancient Proverb

darkjoke.thought:
I told my girlfriend she was drawing her eyebrows too high.
She looked surprised.

My dad said he wanted to be cremated. I said that's beautiful, honoring his wishes.
He said, "I'm not dead yet." I said, "I know, but why wait?"
I'm reading a book on the history of glue. I can't put it down.

My therapist asked why I always assume the worst.
I said, "That way I'm never disappointed." She said, "That's not how therapy works."
I said, "Exactly."

I went to a restaurant that serves breakfast at any time.
So I ordered French toast during the Holocaust.

My friend said depression is just a chemical imbalance.
I said, "Yeah, and the Titanic was just a boat with a moisture problem."

I have an stepson now. His dad left when he was young.
I asked my wife how she explained it to him. She said, "I told him Daddy had to go find himself."
I said, "Did you mention he's still looking?"

People keep telling me I'm in denial.
I'm not in denial. You're in denial.

My doctor told me I need to watch my drinking.
So now I drink in front of a mirror.

I said to my wife, "I think you're overreacting to my affair."
She said, "I'm leaving you." I said, "See? Overreacting."

My friend asked if I believe in life after death.
I said, "No, but I believe in debt after death. My creditors are very committed."

I used to think I had commitment issues.
Turns out I just have excellent self-awareness.

My therapist said I use humor as a defense mechanism.
I said, "That's ridiculous." We both laughed. Then I cried alone in my car.

I told my wife she was being irrational.
She asked me to name one irrational thing she'd done.
I said, "You married me."

My friend said he's finally getting his life together.
I said, "That's great!" He said, "Yeah, I got a storage unit."

I went to my doctor about my memory loss.
He said, "When did it start?" I said, "When did what start?"

People say money can't buy happiness.
But it can buy a jet ski. Have you ever seen someone frowning on a jet ski?
You have? That's probably a different problem.

I told my boss I was feeling burnt out.
He said, "You should take a vacation." I said, "From what? This job or my life?"
He said, "Yes."

My friend became a life coach after his own life fell apart.
I said, "How is that working out?" He said, "Great! Turns out people pay for pessimism if you call it realism."

I don't believe in astrology.
I'm a Capricorn and we're very skeptical.
